description: Tan paper in banded layers, one dark doorway low on the side. Prised out of a Stumpling's moss, and empty. Mostly.
lore: Boiled down it makes a passable paper, grey and tough, and that is the whole reason a nest is worth twenty-six gold while a handful of moss is worth nothing. The bands are worth more than the paper to the right buyer: one band a season, so a nest the size of a head has been building for eleven years, and the [[monsters/tree_stump|Stumpling]] carrying it has been standing in one spot that long. Put a stick in the doorway before it goes in your bag. Then wait. The man who taught everyone that rule is the man who did not.
gm_notes: How to date a Stumpling by its lodger. The last line is the joke and the warning at once; the hornets are never described and should not be.
